The video starts with the TEDx Rainier logo displayed on a black background, with "x = independently" below the text. The scene then transitions to a man with a shaved head wearing a white and light-blue striped button-down shirt. The man is speaking and gesturing with his hands, moving a remote clicker around as he speaks. A microphone is attached near his right cheek. The background features artwork, including one painting with a pink and purple abstract landscape. He introduces himself as Joe Justice, a software consultant and a member of Team Wiki Speed. He shares that the team has built a fast, affordable, ultra-efficient commuter car, a picture of which then shows up as a red open-top car labeled with "Efficiency" and "104 MPG" next to it. He then returns to describing that mainstream hybrid cars only improve by 2 MPG every six years. A picture of three cars, all the same model with minor differences in appearance, appear with the description of the mileage. He expresses the expensive and lengthy process that exists in existing manufacturing processes when design updates are desired by showing a mold and a statement that an engineer would have to wait ten years to implement those updates. The video continues with a diagram titled "MANUFACTURING, AND OLD SOFTWARE TEAMS" and notes that new products are based on "what we believed the customer wanted, 10 years ago".
